Backfilling is one of the messiest things in data engineering.
Yet every engineering team eventually has to face it.

A backfill is, in a nutshell, the retroactive reload of historical data after schema changes, logic fixes or data reprocessing jobs.

It can be painful because... 🚨 
⇀ It can break hundreds of downstream pipelines.
⇀ It requires validation, coordination & precision.
⇀ It is hard to validate and harder to roll back.
⇀ It is normally done under tight deadlines.

But when done right... ✅ 
⇀ It’s clean. 
⇀ It's fast. 
⇀ And almost invisible.

~~~~

This infographic introduces the two most common backfilling strategies and breaks down the “Shell Game” one, used for small, safe backfills.

The kind you can pull off without burning everything down. 😉 

Once taught during Zach Wilson's YT bootcamp 🙌
